TIPPED. DIVING. CAUGHT. 😲🏈

The defender got a hand on it — and it still wasn’t enough.

A Texas high school deep shot gets deflected at the catch point… and #5 in white re-tracks it in under a second, lays out at full stretch, and pulls it in about a foot off the turf at the 11-yard line.

THE BIOMECHANICS (digitized from the film):
• Throw: ≈38 yards in the air
• Tip → catch: under 1 second (27 frames of film)
• Front knee at full extension: 179° — dead straight
• Hip closes to 80° as he reaches
• Trail knee tucks to 53° at the catch, so nothing drags the ball loose
• Ball secured ≈1 ft off the ground and held through the roll

Angles were digitized frame-by-frame from the film (±5°) — film estimates, not lab data. The clip’s playback looks slowed, so the reaction time is counted in film frames, not real-world seconds.

6-3, 245, and 57 career rushing touchdowns, which set the SEC record.

Tim Tebow at Florida, a quarterback who ran like a fullback. Roboflow pose tracking shows the mechanics behind the power.

The Speed Doctor breakdown:
1. The carry. Roboflow pose: trunk ~36° forward, both knees bent ~110° (2D). Low pad level, so the first defender meets his shoulder, not his chest.
2. The goal-line pile. Feet keep driving through contact. At ~8 mph and 245 lbs he brings ~400 kg·m/s of momentum (estimated), about what a 300-lb lineman carries at 6.5 mph.
3. The open-field stride. Trunk ~20°, front knee ~91°, drive leg ~156° (2D). Still leaning in, ready to lower a shoulder.

Listed vs. estimated: 6-3/245 and 57 rushing TDs are per Florida's roster page. Angles are Roboflow 2D pose. Speeds and momentum are Speed Doctor estimates from a highlight montage.

Down 28-12 at halftime. Third play of the second half: 80 yards.

Texas QB Vince Young at Oklahoma State in 2005. At 6-5 and 233, Roboflow pose tracking shows how that frame covers ground.

The Speed Doctor breakdown:
1. The escape. He slips outside the rush and turns his shoulders downfield in a couple of steps. The decision comes first; the stride does the rest.
2. The pursuit. The Cowboys defender chases from behind and the gap grows every stride. About 12 seconds from snap to end zone: a ~14 mph average, scramble included (estimated).
3. The stride. Roboflow pose: trunk ~7°, drive leg fully extended at ~179° (2D). Estimated near 20 mph.

Reported vs. estimated: 6-5/233 is his Texas roster listing; the 80-yard TD, 267 rushing yards and 47-28 final are per Texas Athletics. Angles are Roboflow 2D pose. Speeds are Speed Doctor estimates from the broadcast clock and film.
